> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86350e125d5773af80fee702766ef19447294557` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca7a649d71aadcad73bc60d31e1ca434c5276c85` — the merge of head `d6a464ce03f8f9a767155addc2ac5ce9bbd74aac` into base `86350e125d5773af80fee702766ef19447294557`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca7a649d71aadcad73bc60d31e1ca434c5276c85 && git checkout ca7a649d71aadcad73bc60d31e1ca434c5276c85
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 86350e125d5773af80fee702766ef19447294557 d6a464ce03f8f9a767155addc2ac5ce9bbd74aac && git checkout -B drift-repro 86350e125d5773af80fee702766ef19447294557 && git merge --no-ff d6a464ce03f8f9a767155addc2ac5ce9bbd74aac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 86350e125d5773af80fee702766ef19447294557
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 86350e125d5773af80fee702766ef19447294557` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-addressed-route.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-address.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-dispatch-status.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`resyncFlowsFromProtocol`), packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx, content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx, skills/objectstack-automation

PR #34048, cards #33893 and #33905, net diff against `main` (merge-base `03b4d2d1`), 6 files, +432/-28. Check-runs on the head: 35 success, 16 skipped (opt-in or UI lanes), none failed or pending; `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test Core` 1-8 and the type-check lanes are all green. The verdict below rests on the tree, read at the head, not on those.

### ① Derived judgments

#33905 (commit `998cb968`), a flow whose one holder's package is disabled while the engine still holds its slot:

- `triggerRun` asks `isDisabledHolderSlot` for every slot that has a package, before the unshared short-cut to `execute`. Right. It is the ruling's fire-time gate, asked at fire time, so a re-enable dispatches with no re-arm; a package-less slot never reaches the question (condition 3).
- `resolveFlowKey` (the run's read only, `durable` excluded) and `servedBareFlowKey` answer `absent` / `undefined` through `isDisabledSoleHolder`. Right. `execute`, `getFlow` and `toggleFlow` are the three entries condition 1 names, and `bareFlowKey` (version history, removal, rollback), `flowDispatchHolder`, the slot table and the run keys are untouched (condition 2).
- The predicate needs both readings of the one resolver (own holding resolved, and `not-found` on the served-caller read), so a slot whose package the registry does not hold, and an engine with no resolver, stay served. Right (condition 3, both pinned as CONTROLs).
- The bare doors that probe `getFlow` first answer `404`. Right, and it is the namespaced address's answer on `main`: `automation-address.ts` returns `404 … not found in namespace` when no served holder holds the name.
- `execute` is gated for every caller, `subflow` and `map` calls included. Right: it is the answer the same call gets once the disable's re-sync has withdrawn the flow, and the answer the shared-name rule already gives (`servedCaller`).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` where the card's condition 5 and the claim wrote `yes`. Right as the dev wrote it for the declared rows: `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as a diff that also widens, and none of the declared rows widens. S1 below is the one place the tree does widen an accept set, undeclared.

#33893 (commit `9d712d1d`), the served holder beside a disabled co-holder:

- `FlowSlotTable.add` files the first package slot under `PACKAGE/NAME` while `coHeldByDisabled`; `remove` moves no key while it holds. Right for the two observed paths of the card (boot pull beside a disabled holder; the disable's re-sync withdrawing the disabled holder's slot), and it is amendment 7's "moves no key".
- `loneSharedFlowKey` now needs the SERVED read to refuse, so the engine's `[M1]` rule (decline, warning, `recordFlowRefusal`, `getFlowRegistration`) stays for two served holders and a disabled co-holder is no `[M1]` case. Right. Two served holders at the boot pull still take `main`'s path (bare key, decline, re-key by the second), unchanged.
- `isShared` reads a lone slot filed under its qualified key as shared. Wrong as built: see F1. It serves the two entries the new pin asks (`execute`, `getFlow`) and turns every other bare reader of the name into a refusal.
- A served holder whose slot was filed bare before the registry held the disabled co-holder keeps the bare key and is now armed (the `[M1]` narrowing covers it). Right, and the later enable still moves that key as on `main`; the changeset's "no re-arm of the served one" holds for the two orders the pins measure.

Public surface: no export, schema key, route or config key is added, removed or re-shaped. `FlowSlotTable`'s constructor takes a second optional parameter (engine-local class).

### ② Semver level

Both changesets are `patch` on `@objectstack/service-automation`; the diff moves no metadata key, so `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` are the level AGENTS.md step 3 gives a non-protocol change, breaking or not.

- `.changeset/33905-disabled-sole-holder-flow.md`: title carries `!`, body carries line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, the moved answers as before/now pairs, the remedy "enable the package", and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which is true: no stored row, key or binding moves.
- `.changeset/33893-served-holder-keeps-slot-key.md`: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no banner, no marker. Correct for a fix, and not yet true of this head: F1 is a set of served answers this commit takes away.
- PR body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `Skills-docs: none — …` line, the BREAKING banner and the FROM → TO table; the title carries `!`. The `Skills-docs:` reason is true: `skills/objectstack-automation` names a disabled package only for a packaged flow's `queue` approver, and no page under `content/docs` outside the release-owned pages states what a trigger or a bare automation entry does for a disabled package's flow.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches the declared rows of #33905. It does not cover F1 (an undeclared narrowing inside the `Clause-②: no` commit) or S1 (an undeclared 409 → accepted at the clone door).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6898330736, `open_questions`: none. Deviations, each answered:

1. Pins as top-level `describe`s in the shared harness files, not per-card files: accepted (AGENTS.md shared-harness rule).
2. The changeset says "ran … It now answers …" in place of FROM → TO labels, because the ADR-0087 gate reads the label as a migration prescription; the PR body keeps the table: accepted, condition 5's rows are present on both carriers.
3. `execute` gated for every caller: accepted, judged right in ①.
4. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` left to CI: accepted, `Lint · ESLint` and the other lint check-runs are green on this head.
5. No second merge of `origin/main`: accepted; none of the six paths moved on `main` since the merge-base.
6. Branch merged `origin/main` after PR #33890 landed, PR opened on `main`: accepted; the net diff is the two card commits.

Out-of-scope finding (the boot pull's first of two SERVED holders declined behind the refused-body warning until the second registers): confirmed as predating this PR and unchanged by it (`coHeldByDisabled` is false while the served read refuses); the seat's request 6898645381 names its follow-up, #34051.

"Parked-run resume is NOT decided here" is stated on the PR body and the changeset, as condition 2 orders. Condition 6's order (PR #33890 first, CONTROL flipped here) holds: the `[#33748]` single-holder CONTROL is the flipped pin.

The PR is still a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself (#33905) is the published rule made real, not a capability taken away. `main` already publishes "A disabled package holds no name" for the flow doors (18.5 notes; `automation-address.ts`; ADR-0150 D3), the disable's re-sync already withdraws a disabled package's flows (sole holders included), and the namespaced address already answers `404`. What this PR removes is the window in which a failed or skipped re-sync left such a flow firing and served bare. The gate is exact on the three entries and the trigger: it asks the one resolver, it gates only a slot whose package the registry holds and has disabled, and nothing durable is re-keyed. I could not make it gate a package-less flow, a flow of an enabled package, or a slot the registry does not hold, and I could not make a disabled sole holder's flow run through `execute`, a subflow call or its trigger.

F1 (must-fix) — #33893 leaves the served holder stuck under its qualified key after the disabled co-holder is uninstalled, and every bare entry that reads `isShared` without the resolver then refuses a name ONE package holds, until a restart. Sequence, all on the normal path: packages A and B both ship flow `t`; disable B; the disable's re-sync calls `withdrawFlowSlot(B, 't')` (`remove` moves no key, A stays `A/t`); uninstall B; the uninstall's re-sync re-registers A's flow, and `placeFlowSlot` returns A's own key, so nothing folds it back. From then on `flowSlots.isShared('t')` is true by the new clause alone (`[...packages.values()][0] !== name`) while the registry holds `t` once. Read in the head's `engine.ts`:
  - `bareFlowKey('t')` throws `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`, whose candidates (`sharedFlowNameRefusal`, read over the slots because the durable read no longer refuses) name A alone: `unregisterFlow('t')` (so `DELETE /automation/t`), `getFlowVersionHistory('t')`, `rollbackFlow('t')` and `withdrawFlow('t')` answer an "ambiguous" 409 that names one package.
  - `inboundHookSlot('t')` with no address answers `refused`, so the bare inbound hook of `t` (`trigger-api` `handleInboundHook`) is not served; external posts to the bare hook URL get the door's one refusal.
  - the credential source's `at('t')` throws the same refusal, and `packagedFlowOwner('t')` answers none.
  On `main` the same sequence folds A's slot to `t` at the withdraw, and after the uninstall `heldByMany` is false, the re-sync re-arms it, and every one of those entries serves the bare name. The new pin "the disabled holder then uninstalled" asserts `flowSlotKey(P1, 't')` is `P1/t` and asks only `execute`, `getFlow` and the trigger, so it fixes the stuck key in place and does not see the refused entries. The CONTROL beside it (uninstall before the withdraw folds back) shows the answer now depends on whether the package was disabled before it was uninstalled. This is a narrowing of served answers inside the commit declared `Clause-②: no`, not named in either changeset. Either fold a lone qualified slot back to its bare key (through `moveFlowRecords`, as an uninstall does today) once the registry no longer holds the name under two packages, or stop reading such a slot as shared at the entries above; then pin `getFlowVersionHistory`, `unregisterFlow` and the bare `inboundHookSlot` for the disable → withdraw → uninstall order.

S1 (should-fix) — #33905 moves three runtime door answers the FROM → TO rows do not carry, because those doors ask `getFlow` a durable question ("is this name taken", "what do I restore") and now get the served answer for a slot the engine still holds. Read in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` at the head (no runtime source changes; the PR body says these were "not measured beyond the table"):
  - the clone door's name-taken probe `getFlow(targetName)`: FROM `409` name taken TO the copy is admitted, and `registerFlow` lands its package-less body in the disabled package's slot, so the package's flow runs the copy's body on re-enable until the next re-sync. This is an accept-set widening under a `no` declaration, and the shadow the same-name refusal exists to prevent.
  - `registerAndSaveFlow`'s `held` (the rollback copy): `null`, so a refused save or landing calls `unregisterFlow(name)` and drops the package's registration where `main` restored it; `keepStoredFlowCredentials` carries nothing forward.
  - `DELETE /automation/NAME`: `flowIsUnknown` is true, the engine's registration is still removed (`unregisterFlow` reads `bareFlowKey`, over every holder), and the door answers `404` unless a stored row was reset, where `main` answered a deletion.
  Each equals what the door answers once the re-sync has withdrawn the flow, which is why this is not a must-fix; but condition 2 keeps durable reads over every holder and condition 5 orders the rows. The claim bars `runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, so: add the three rows to the changeset and the PR body, change `Clause-②` only if the seat rules the clone row a widening that the line must carry, and file the collision-probe and rollback-copy reads as a follow-up card.

N1 (nit) — the door list on both carriers names `POST /automation/NAME/clone`, and the runtime pin's `DOORS` table has five rows without it; the clone source-404 row is declared and unpinned. Prose or follow-up.

N2 (nit) — the runtime describe passes on `main` as well (its service double is hand-set to the new answers); the PR body says so and names A3 as the moving half. Accepted as stated.

Delta owed: F1's fix and S1's rows, on the new head.
